instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: Twenty and a regular in the back four through the record run of fourteen straight clean sheets; a clear step up on the loan season.
Four goals and seven assists from right-back in a side that won the league with 81 points; one of the best attacking full-backs in Europe that season.
Lost his place to Tim Flowers in November.
Twenty-seven league goals at twenty-one in a side built around Cristiano Ronaldo; elite movement and finishing, not yet the complete centre-forward.
His one season as an undisputed first choice, and good enough in a relegated side to earn a Manchester United move as understudy.
Captain of a treble-winning side and eleven league assists from full-back; the best right-back in the world at this point.
Signed from Atletico Madrid and a capable squad player for the champions at 22; the minutes reflect the competition ahead of him, not his level.
Lost the left-back place over the course of the relegation season; the pace and the crossing were already going at twenty-eight.
Twelve goals and an England cap at twenty-two; the ability was briefly genuine, which the following two seasons do not reflect.
The season was ended in October by a broken leg. Rated as the France international and twice Ligue 1 top scorer he was at twenty-two: frightening pace and a real finish, raw everywhere else.
His one fit season, in the eighty-six-point side: a left foot good enough that the dead-ball delivery alone kept him in the team.
Nineteen and physically ready enough to deputise in a Champions League back four; strong and brave in the air, badly exposed by pace.
His best Arsenal season: a regular in the back four that went ten Champions League ties without conceding.
Three starts in a season after two years of loans and injuries; still strong in the air, still undone by anything quick.
A Champions League winner and a Serie A forward for most of the previous decade; twelve goals in twenty-six starts at thirty, when fit, which was rarely.
World player of the year and the outstanding midfielder on the planet; one of the handful of genuinely all-time-great seasons in the database.
Thirty-two, and two seasons on, in a Madrid side that won nothing; still the best passer on the pitch but no longer able to run a game for ninety minutes.
Thirty-three and a substitute in a promoted side; honest running and nothing else at top-flight level.
A slow start and then the best creative player in the league from Christmas onwards; already close to the level he held through the title season.
An ever-present for a side relegated with 34 points; a promising young keeper whose shot-stopping was ahead of his handling and command of the area.
Frozen out and released in January after the Turkey–England fallout; four starts, and rated as a player who had stopped playing rather than one who had declined that far.
Technically the best of Liverpool’s attacking players that season and decisive in Europe; erratic week to week, which is what keeps him out of the elite band.
